title: Finite subsets of torsion-free DVR comodules lie in finite free subcomodules
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $C$ be an $A$-module flat over $A$, meaning that tensoring with $C$ preserves injections of $A$-modules, with $A$-linear maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_A C$ and $\epsilon:C\to A$ satisfying coassociativity and both counit identities. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $M$ be a torsion-free $A$-module, meaning $am=0$ with $a\ne0$ implies $m=0$, with an $A$-linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_A C$ satisfying $(\rho\otimes1_C)\rho=(1_M\otimes\Delta)\rho$ and $(1_M\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_M$. For every finite subset $T\subseteq M$, there exist an $A$-submodule $V\subseteq M$ containing $T$, a finite $A$-basis of $V$, and a coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_A C$ satisfying the same identities, such that $(i\otimes1_C)\rho_V=\rho i$ for the inclusion $i:V\hookrightarrow M$. The empty subset and the zero module are allowed.

source.place: Milne, Basic Theory of Affine Group Schemes, VIII, Aside 4.7, printed p.117, together with Aside 9.4, printed pp.125--126 (the finite torsion-free module is free over a DVR). WANTED local copy; read https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf. No field-only subcomodule lemma is being applied.

proof.text: For each $t\in T$ choose a finite tensor expansion $\rho(t)=\sum_{a\in I_t}m_{ta}\otimes c_{ta}$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $W\subseteq M$ be the span of the finite union of all $m_{ta}$. Then $W$ is finitely generated and $\rho(t)$ belongs to the image of $W\otimes_A C$ for every $t\in T$. If $T$ is empty take $W=0$. No basis of $C$ is chosen.

source.place: VIII, Aside 4.7, printed p.117: choose a finite coefficient module and take its stable core; Aside 9.4, printed pp.125--126, integral representation application.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-coalgebra-subcomodule-core] to the ring $A$, coalgebra $C$, comodule $(M,\rho)$ and this $W$. Its flatness and coaction hypotheses are exactly those of the item. Put $V=W^\circ$. Its statement gives $V\subseteq W$, a coaction $\rho_V$ satisfying both identities, and $(i\otimes1_C)\rho_V=\rho i$. The expansions in step 1 imply $t\in W^\circ$ for each $t\in T$, hence $T\subseteq V$.

source.place: VIII, Aside 4.7, printed p.117: choose a finite coefficient module and take its stable core; Aside 9.4, printed pp.125--126, integral representation application.

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] every ideal of $A$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $A$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Now $W$ is finite by construction and $V\subseteq W$ by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] with ambient module $W$ to conclude that $V$ is finitely generated.

source.place: VIII, Aside 4.7, printed p.117: choose a finite coefficient module and take its stable core; Aside 9.4, printed pp.125--126, integral representation application.

proof.text: If $av=0$ in $V$ with $a\ne0$, inclusion in $M$ gives $a i(v)=0$, so torsion-freeness of $M$ and injectivity of $i$ give $v=0$. Thus $V$ is torsion free. By [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free], $V$ is finite free and has a finite $A$-basis. Together with step 2 this supplies every required datum. For $T=\varnothing$, step 1 gives $W=0$ and step 2 gives $V\subseteq0$, so $V=0$ with its empty basis and zero coaction. The same applies when $M=0$.

source.place: VIII, Aside 4.7, printed p.117: choose a finite coefficient module and take its stable core; Aside 9.4, printed pp.125--126, integral representation application.
